17.0.0.en: The Lord spoke to Moses, the leader of the people, to instruct Aaron and his sons, so that they might understand and teach the people the manner and the place of slaughtering the sacrifices.

17.1.0.en: There are two opinions in the interpretation of these two verses:

17.1.1.en: 1- That the talk here is about the children of Israel slaughtering animals for food while they are in the wilderness of Sinai, so they bring their sacrifices and slaughter them before the tabernacle of the congregation. But when they moved to the Promised Land, many of the tribes came to live far from the tabernacle of the congregation or the Temple of Solomon, so they slaughtered in their cities what they needed to eat (Deut 12:20-22). What was slaughtered for food in the wilderness was little, since they depended for the most part on eating the manna, as is shown by the fact that they asked God for meat and He gave them quail (Ex 16:12); consequently, their coming to the tabernacle of the congregation to slaughter what they would eat seldom happened.

17.1.2.en: 2- What is meant here is what is offered as sacrifices to God, that is, peace offerings, and it is required that the sacrifices be offered in one place, the tabernacle of the congregation, and whoever does not do this is put to death. This word of God is of great importance, for these reasons:

17.1.3.en: 1- Keeping them away from the worship of idols and from slaughtering to them, so that worship is offered to God alone.

17.1.4.en: 2- Attachment to the house of the Lord, where they bring all their requests.

17.1.5.en: 3- Adherence to one rite in offering the sacrifices, to establish one set of spiritual thoughts.

17.1.6.en: 4- Unity among the people, since all offer their sacrifices in one place.

17.1.7.en: 5- Giving the priests a portion of the sacrifices as their food.

17.1.8.en: 6- Giving the Lord a portion of their sacrifices, that He may bless their lives.

17.1.9.en: So everyone who wants to slaughter, whether inside the place where the tents of the children of Israel are or outside it, must come to slaughter before the tabernacle of the congregation, and whoever slaughters in another place is counted as a shedder of blood or a murderer and must be put to death. But there are some scattered events in the Holy Bible in which sacrifices were offered on special altars other than the altar of the tabernacle of the congregation, in obedience to orders from God and for spiritual purposes that God willed, as in the case of Gideon (Judg 6:25-27), Samuel the prophet (1 Sam 7:5-11), David the prophet (2 Sam 24:

17.2.0.en: These sacrifices, of which the people will eat, are what are called peace offerings, and the one who offers them takes care to offer the fat to God, which the priest lifts onto the altar, and likewise the blood is sprinkled around the altar, because the fat is the richest part of the sacrifice and the blood represents the life of the sacrifice, so they are offered to God, as the rite of the peace offering prescribes (ch. 3).

17.3.0.en: The Egyptians and some other countries offered sacrifices to animals such as the calf Apis, so God forbids them to offer sacrifices to the goats that they worship. These idolatrous worships were connected with fornication, so God warns them against them, and the offering of sacrifices is restricted to God alone at the tabernacle of the congregation.

17.3.1.en: Know that you are wholly consecrated to God, so do not give your thoughts or your time to the world and to evil, so that your effort may be spent on the love of God and the love of others.

17.4.0.en: God stresses that all the sacrifices or burnt offerings offered to God are to be at the tabernacle of the congregation and not in any other place. This applies to the Jew or the non-Jew who has joined the people of God and believed in Him and wants to offer a sacrifice.

17.5.0.en: God forbade His people to drink blood, for the following reasons:

17.5.1.en: 1- Because blood represents the life of the animal, which belongs to God and not to a human being.

17.5.2.en: 2- The blood is offered on the altar to God, as it signifies the blood of Christ, who makes atonement for us.

17.5.3.en: This applies to the children of Israel or the strangers dwelling among them, and whoever breaks this commandment is cut off from the people, that is, he is set apart from it and loses his membership in the people of God because he treated His commandments lightly.

17.5.4.en: Do not make light of the commandments of God and justify your errors, lest God abandon you and you lose His blessing in your life; and know that all God's commandments are for your good, so do not be drawn after the pleasures of your sinful self.

17.6.0.en: If they hunt an animal of the clean animals that are permitted to be eaten, but which is not of the kind that is offered as sacrifices to God, such as deer, then when they slaughter it to eat it, they must pour out its blood and drain it and then cover this blood with dust, for the following reasons:

17.6.1.en: 1- Out of respect for the blood, which represents the life of the animal that God created.

17.6.2.en: 2- Because the animal, like man, is made of dust and returns to dust.

17.6.3.en: 3- Lest the blood be used in offering it to idolatrous worship.

17.7.0.en: He also warned them not to eat an animal that was torn by a wild beast or died in any accident, because a large part of its blood is still in it. Whoever knows that the animal is dead or a prey and eats of it, that is, insists on breaking the commandment, is cut off from the people of God.

17.8.0.en: If a person of the people of God eats of an animal that died or was torn by a wild beast and did not know this, and thought it was an animal slaughtered in the ordinary way, he becomes unclean for two reasons:

17.8.1.en: 1- Because he drank blood retained inside the prey.

17.8.2.en: 2- Because he ate flesh that the unclean beast had touched.

17.8.3.en: So he must bathe and wash his clothes and remain unclean until the evening, and whoever does not do so is punished according to the judgment of the elders of Israel.

17.8.4.en: Forbidden marriages and sexual perversions: general introduction

17.8.5.en: In the first ten chapters, the Book of Leviticus showed the hideousness of sin, which needed many sacrifices to make atonement for it, and these are aspects of the sacrifice of the Cross.

17.8.6.en: Then it presented practical laws on holiness in food and drink, clothing, dwelling and health in (ch. 11-15).

17.8.7.en: Then it presented the great Day of Atonement, which signifies the day of the Cross, and the law of slaughtering and the importance of blood (ch. 16, 17).

17.8.8.en: Then in the coming chapters it speaks about the importance of holiness in dealing with God and with others, and the holiness of the priests (ch. 18-22).

18.0.0.en: Before God gives them His laws of holiness, He declares to them that He is their God, and this means:

18.0.1.en: 1- Their attachment to Him alone and not to the idol gods.

18.0.2.en: 2- His love for them, His care for them and His concern for their holiness.

18.0.3.en: 3- The fear of Him and adherence to His ordinances so that they are not punished.

18.1.0.en: God warns them against imitating the Egyptians in their idolatrous worships and customs, which they came to know during all their dwelling in Egypt. He also warns them against accepting the ideas of the Canaanite peoples, whom they will drive out and settle around them in the Promised Land, and against mixing with them and being defiled by their ideas. Rather, they are to hold fast only to the laws of God, their only God, and apply them and live by them and enjoy His care for them.

18.1.1.en: God's commandments are not mere orders; they give you a pure, happy life with Him. So take care to apply the words of the Holy Bible in your life, and do not be content with theoretical knowledge, so that you may taste fellowship with God through His living word in you.

18.2.0.en: Nakedness: the reproductive organs; what is meant by uncovering them is marriage and having physical relations. Here he warns against marrying close relatives. This was permitted before the Law of Moses, yet the Law of Moses is still applied in Christianity, and even increased in a few of its provisions, for the following reasons:

18.2.1.en: 1- Preserving the purity of the feelings of fatherhood, sonship and brotherhood, apart from sex.

18.2.2.en: 2- From the health standpoint, this is better for avoiding diseases and troubles that result in the offspring.

18.2.3.en: And God specifies these forbidden close kinships in the following verses.

18.3.0.en: He forbids marrying the father or the mother, or the father's wife or the mother's husband, because the two have become one flesh, and consequently the father's wife has become a mother and the mother's husband is a father. So to preserve the purity of the feelings and dealings of parents and children within the family, the Law forbade these marriages.

18.4.0.en: He also forbids marrying a sister, whether a full sister or a half-sister, of whom he said "born at home, or born abroad," that is, born of another mother or another father, in order to preserve the purity of the feelings and dealings of brothers and sisters together.

18.5.0.en: He also forbids a grandfather to marry his granddaughter, whether the daughter of his son or the daughter of his daughter, in order to preserve the purity of the feelings of fatherhood and sonship.

18.6.0.en: He also forbids marrying the daughter of the father's wife, because she is counted a sister like one born of the father, although she was born to the father's wife by another husband than the father; but by the woman's marriage to the father she became one with him, and consequently the woman's daughter is counted as his daughter, so it is not right to marry her.

18.7.0.en: He also forbids marrying the father's sister or the mother's sister, because she is a sister of the father or the mother and is very close, and is treated as a mother, so it is not right to marry her.

18.8.0.en: Likewise he forbids a girl to marry her maternal uncle or paternal uncle, or a son to marry the wife of his maternal uncle, for she is counted as his aunt, that is, his mother, so it is not right to marry her if her husband dies.

18.9.0.en: He warns against marrying the daughter-in-law, that is, the son's wife, for she is counted as a daughter. The punishment of one who marries or commits adultery with his son's wife was death (ch. 20:12).

18.10.0.en: It is also not right to marry the brother's wife after his death. But the Law of Moses permitted this marriage in one special case, namely if this brother had not begotten children before his death, so his brother marries her to raise up seed and the offspring are reckoned to the dead man so that he may inherit in the Promised Land (Deut 25:5-10). But in Christianity there is no longer a Promised Land but the heavenly Jerusalem, and consequently the Law forbids marrying the brother's wife after his death in all cases.

18.11.0.en: He also forbids marrying a woman and then marrying her daughter too, or her granddaughter, because by marrying the mother he became a father to her daughter and a grandfather to her granddaughter.

18.12.0.en: He also forbids marrying two sisters at the same time, because by this he makes them rivals and problems arise. But it is understood from this that marrying the wife's sister is permitted if the wife dies; in Christian law, however, marrying the wife's sister after her death is not permitted, because she is counted as his sister, in order to preserve the purity of dealings with the wife's sisters.

18.12.1.en: Let your love be pure, your look innocent and your dealings sound with your relatives. Do not be careless in the name of affection to the point of exposing yourself to attacks from Satan. And in proportion to your humility and care, you can live a life of strong, pure love for God's sake and be loved and useful to those around you.

18.13.0.en: God forbids physical relations with the wife during the period of her menstruation (the monthly period), for the following reasons:

18.13.1.en: 1- She was considered unclean, so whoever approached her became unclean for seven days (ch. 15:19-24).

18.13.2.en: 2- It causes diseases and bleeding, so relations at this time are against the woman's health.

18.13.3.en: 3- It does not suit propriety, good taste and general cleanliness.

18.13.4.en: And whoever lies with a woman inadvertently becomes unclean for seven days, but whoever lies with her deliberately, both of them were cut off from the people (ch. 15:19-24).

18.14.0.en: Thy neighbour's wife: that is, his wife.

18.14.1.en: Seed: a physical relation that can produce offspring.

18.14.2.en: He warns against adultery because the Sixth Commandment forbids it (Ex 20), and whoever committed adultery was put to death by stoning (ch. 20:20, Deut 22:22).

18.15.0.en: Molech: the god of the Ammonites, also called Moloch or Milcom or Baal. He is the god of fire, and they offered him human sacrifices of their children, either by roasting them in fire or slaughtering them and then roasting them to please him, so they made them pass through the fire until they were burned, in order that he might be pleased with them.

18.15.1.en: He warns them against offering their children as sacrifices to Molech, because by this idolatrous worship they commit savage acts and declare their allegiance to the idol gods and their rejection of God, and so they profane His name.

18.16.0.en: Here he warns against sexual perversion, that a male lie with a male, and of course also a female with a female, for this is a great uncleanness.

18.17.0.en: Lie down thereto: an animal leaping upon a woman to have a physical relation with her.

18.17.1.en: He also warns them against being inflamed by their desires to the point of clinging to animals in order to have physical relations with them, for this is a great sin and uncleanness.

18.17.2.en: Take care in watching the various media so as not to defile your eyes and mind with the perverse practices of the world, and do not let curiosity draw you to this. It is not logical to desire these terrible evils, and leniency in seeing them may lead to attempting to practice them or justifying them, or at the least to defiling the mind.

18.18.1.en: God warns His people of the punishment that will come upon them if they fall into the preceding sins mentioned in this chapter, whether the perversions or the forbidden marriages. God will be angry with them as He will be angry with the peoples dwelling in Canaan, and will drive them out from before the children of Israel and settle them there in their place; if they sin, they too will be driven out of the land of Canaan, and this is what actually happened in the captivity, when they were driven out of their land and scattered among the kingdoms of the world because of their evils.

18.19.0.en: God calls His people to hold fast to His commandments and also to keep away from these sins mentioned before.

18.20.0.en: God makes clear that the pagan peoples defiled the land with the preceding evils, and if the people of God fall into them, they will defile the land and be exposed to the same fate as the pagan peoples, that the land will cast them out from it, that is, God will drive them out of it.

18.21.2.en: God declares that the souls that fall into these preceding sins will be cut off from the people of God and so lose His care, and may be exposed to death or other punishments; therefore He calls them to keep away from these perversions and evils and to hold fast to His commandments and His worship.

18.21.3.en: Look at the punishment of sin, which is eternal torment, so that you are not careless about the smallest part of it, however much the surrounding circumstances encourage you to it. Do not lose your eternity for these trivial and base things, and know that every striving or renunciation of anything that leads to sin is very precious to God, and He will help you, support you and compensate you with joys that cannot be expressed on earth or in heaven.

19.0.0.en: God requires His people to live in holiness because they are His children, and since He is perfect in holiness, they too must live in it because they are His children. They obtain this holiness through carrying out His commandments, which will be mentioned in the following verses, and through keeping away from the evils, some of which He mentioned in the previous chapter.

19.1.0.en: He requires every person to respect his mother and father, as the Fifth Commandment enjoined (Ex 20). Here he puts the mother before the father to declare the equality of the two in the eyes of the son and in the eyes of God, and because there may be a more affectionate relationship with the mother, yet it does not cancel respect and reverence, whether they are in their youth or in their old age; they give them adequate care and even honor them after their death.

19.1.1.en: He also reminds them of keeping the Sabbath day holy, as the Fourth Commandment enjoined (Ex 20), and likewise the seventh year and the year of Jubilee, that is, the fiftieth (ch. 25:4-12); this means respect for God and setting aside sufficient time for Him to worship Him.

19.2.0.en: He warns them against the worship of idols or making their images, for this is counted as a rejection of the worship of God.

19.3.0.en: The sanctuary of the Lord: the altar of God and His house.

19.3.1.en: If they slaughter peace offerings, of which they offer something to God and eat the rest, let it be eaten on the first and second day of the slaughter of the animal; on the third day this is not permitted, and whoever does so becomes unclean, and if he does so deliberately he is cut off from the people of God, because he wronged the house of God by not carrying out His commands, and this is in the case of a vow or a freewill offering, that is, an additional offering. But if it is a peace offering offered as thanksgiving to God, it is eaten on the day of its slaughter only (ch. 7:11-21).

19.3.2.en: Do you care for your parents and bear with them if they err? Know that honoring them rejoices the heart of God, because by this you declare your love for Him and for them, and also your humility, and so you receive many blessings.

19.4.0.en: Gleaning of thy harvest: what is scattered of the grain on the ground and gathered up.

19.4.1.en: Harvest, or gathering the crops, is a time of joy, so the Law reminds them not to forget the poor. The owner of the field should leave parts, even small ones, of his field in its corners, not reaping all that is in them, so that they may be for the poor to gather for themselves without embarrassment. Likewise what is scattered of the grain on the ground the reapers do not try to gather but leave for the poor and the strangers, that is, all the needy, to glean.

19.5.0.en: Thou shalt not glean it: do not gather the grapes from the field several times, but leave some of them remaining.

19.5.1.en: Every grape of thy vineyard: the scattered grapes that fell on the ground.

19.5.2.en: Likewise the owners of vineyards, when gathering the grapes, do not gather them several times but leave some of the berries on the vines for the poor to gather. And when some grains fall on the ground and are scattered, they leave them also for the needy. Here the Law gives several benefits, which are:

19.5.3.en: 1- The owner of the field or vineyard feels the blessing of God, who stretches out His hand and takes a share from him through His poor children.

19.5.4.en: 2- It fills the hearts of the owners of fields with mercy toward their needy brethren, so they feel their fellowship as one people of God.

19.5.5.en: 3- The poor person does not feel embarrassment, but takes what he needs without asking.

19.5.6.en: 4- Reducing or preventing begging, which troubles the rich as it troubles the poor.

19.6.0.en: The Law forbids some sins such as:

19.6.1.en: 1- Stealing, whether by not returning a trust or by a person taking anything that is not his right.

19.6.2.en: 2- Lying, to gain any gains or to hide a fault, or any deceit.

19.6.3.en: 3- Dealing falsely, meaning treachery, whether by robbing rights or by any deceit, and it may reach murder as in Cain. And when he says "to his neighbour" he means deceit here, as a person finds treachery from one from whom he does not expect it; it is a wrongful exploitation of people's trust to achieve personal ends.

19.7.0.en: In the Old Testament God allowed His people to swear by His name so that they would not swear by the idol gods and so that their faith in Him would be strengthened, but He required the oath to be true, to confirm the absence of lying; and whoever swears falsely in the Old Testament wrongs the name of God and profanes it, because he used it in false speech. But in the New Testament, since the spiritual person has risen higher, he no longer uses the name of God in material dealings, as it is too lofty for that, so he does not swear at all.

19.8.0.en: He forbids employers to exploit or wrong those who work for them: they do not force them to do work beyond their strength or without pay, and they do not rob them of their rights by giving them less than their wages, exploiting their weakness and need, and they do not delay giving them their wages. Though they have the money with them, they delay the wages to the next day, although the hired servant or worker needs it today to meet his needs. That is, He forbids the strong man to use his strength in exploiting and wronging the weak.

19.9.0.en: He warns against exploiting the weakness of the helpless, such as the deaf, that is, one who does not hear, so we curse him, confident that he does not hear and cannot answer us; but his God, who allowed him this helplessness, hears and will take vengeance on us if we do not repent. Whoever wrongs a helpless person wrongs God, who allowed him this helplessness.

19.9.1.en: Likewise whoever puts a stumbling block in the way of a blind man, such as a stone or an obstacle, so that he trips and falls over it, God is very angry with him, so we must keep before us the fear of God and awe of Him, because He defends His helpless children and avenges them.

19.10.0.en: Here he addresses not only rulers and judges but every person, to judge with justice in all matters brought before him and not to wrong anyone, and to take care not to be deceived by the appearance of a poor man who looks weak but in truth has committed a crime; when his tears flow or he speaks in a low voice, this should not affect justice. On the other hand, do not pervert judgment and be lenient with a person of high standing, out of respect for him, acquitting him of a wrong he committed or wronging another.

19.11.0.en: What is meant by the talebearer is words of condemnation that wrong others, so the Law forbids carrying words of condemnation and spreading them, because it is a wrong against God, the Creator of those whom he condemns, besides a weakness of love toward them. He also warns against making light of the lives of others, which is represented by their blood, for example by not testifying to save them from death or danger, or leaving injustice to fall on them, or by bearing false witness against them or clearly wronging them; in this a person stands and tramples on the blood of his neighbor by his passivity.

19.12.0.en: He requires His people to love one another, and that no one carry hatred for anyone in his heart; and if someone wrongs another, let him go to him and rebuke him and admonish him (warn him), so that peace may return between them and he may always keep a pure heart toward everyone.

19.13.0.en: If any person of the people of God wrongs you, do not be angry with him and hate him and try to take revenge on him, but love him as yourself, because he is a member with you in the people of God, and every person of course loves himself and fears for himself. So one should love others as he loves himself, and have compassion on them if they err, and forgive them.

19.14.1.en: God calls them to keep all His commandments, whether great ones or what seems small, as in the verse; all of them are important and have useful spiritual and material meanings.

19.14.2.en: So He forbids them to pair two kinds of animals, that is, not to carry out crossbreeding, and likewise not to sow the field with two kinds of crops, and also not to make their garments of two fabrics such as linen and wool, for the following reasons:

19.14.3.en: 1- A person, if he mates two animals of two kinds and produces a new animal, may think that he is a creator and shares with God in divinity.

19.14.4.en: 2- When two kinds are sown in one field, it is very hard to care for them together because of the differing needs for irrigation, fertilizing and harvesting.

19.14.5.en: 3- Wearing garments of two fabrics may cause some troubles to the skin.

19.14.6.en: And the spiritual meaning of this is not to mix the thoughts of the world with spiritual thoughts, with the importance of concentrating on one spiritual thought, for example not being distracted during prayer by thoughts about service.

19.15.1.en: Redeemed: her price is paid, that is, her redemption, to her owner, so that she becomes his possession and his maidservant.

19.15.2.en: Freedom given: her owner and master gave her to this suitor free of charge.

19.15.3.en: If a free man betroths a bondmaid and intends to pay her price so that she becomes his maidservant, but before he pays her price or her master gives her to him, he goes too far in playing with her until he commits adultery with her, the law of adultery, putting them to death (Deut 22:23), is not applied to them. This is because she is first the property of a master, and the ownership of this master must be respected and no loss caused him; and on the other hand, this man is her betrothed and intended to buy her so that she would become his wife like one of his concubines, that is, his maidservants whom he married. So the judges, that is, the elders of Israel, give them a sentence of discipline, most likely scourging.

19.16.0.en: After the discipline of the betrothed pair, the free betrothed man must offer a sacrifice for his trespass before God, which is a ram, because adultery is a grave sin directed against God even if the betrothed pair consented to this lying together. Here is a clear declaration of the need for the blood of Christ the Redeemer, whom this sacrifice signifies, for the removal of sin.

19.16.1.en: As for the betrothed bondmaid, because she owns nothing, she is exempted from offering the sacrifice and offers repentance only.

19.16.2.en: May you consider the feelings of others and not wrong them; put yourself in their place, and what you do not accept for yourself, do not do to them. And if you wrong them, offer repentance to God, apologize to them, and compensate them as much as you can for what they lost.

19.17.0.en: Uncircumcised: the tree is figuratively counted as uncircumcised, that is, not belonging to the people of God and not blessed by Him.

19.17.1.en: Uncircumcised: that is, not circumcised, and this meaning too is figurative, meaning that its fruit is not to be eaten.

19.17.2.en: This commandment concerns their life when they enter the Promised Land and plant a tree to yield fruit to be eaten, and this is of course apart from the trees planted by the original inhabitants of the land and apart from trees that do not yield fruit for eating. The commandment prescribes leaving the fruit for three years without eating of it, because the fruit of new trees is not fit to eat in the first three years, in addition to the fact that some pagan peoples offered the fruit of their trees at the start of planting to the idol gods, so their leaving these fruits declares their rejection of these idolatrous worships.

19.18.0.en: Before they eat of the fruit, they must receive the blessing of God, so they offer the fruit of the fourth year to God, and the priests and the Levites eat it.

19.19.0.en: In the fifth year and afterward they are permitted to eat the fruit, and it is blessed by God, and by this they declare their allegiance to Him and their enjoyment of His care.

19.19.1.en: Be careful to offer to God from your money and your various gifts, so that you may receive His blessing in your life, for a little blessed by God is better than much without blessing; and by this you also show your love for others.

19.20.0.en: He warns them against eating meat with its blood, that is, meat from which the blood has not been drained, out of respect for blood, which signifies the life of man, besides the fact that it stirs up the passions (ch. 17:14). The pagans used to dip meat in blood or drink it to please the gods.

19.20.1.en: He also warns them against imitating the pagans in optimism and pessimism, that is, being hopeful if they see or hear a sound and, on the contrary, expecting evil if they hear or see other things. All these are of course superstitions connected with pagan worships.

19.20.2.en: In addition to that, he warned them against divination, that is, searching for the future by astrology and various methods of charlatanry such as casting shells or asking sorcerers.

19.21.0.en: The men among some pagan peoples used to cut the hair of their heads round, leaving only a circle of hair on top of the head. Others tampered with the two sides of the beard, that is, the sideburns, cutting them and leaving a lower part around the chin. So God forbids them all these practices that the pagan peoples do to please their gods.

19.22.0.en: Some of the pagans, in excess of grief, used to cut their bodies as a sign of the loss of their hope and their loss on account of the departed one, so God commanded His people to keep away from this despair and its practices. He also commanded them not to make a mark, that is, marks by branding on the body, for the forms of some pagan gods, that is, to keep away from all pagan ideas.

19.23.0.en: Familiar spirits: evil spirits, that is, demons.

19.23.1.en: Wizards: evil spirits, since some think there are spirits that follow people and can harm them. He forbids them to believe in and seek the demons who take the form of familiar spirits or followers, and likewise those who deal with demons, who are called soothsayers; whoever contacts and deals with demons defiles himself and defies God, therefore He says "I am the Lord," that is, He warns them to fear. This is mentioned often in the Holy Bible, as in (Isa 8:19, Eph 5:11).

19.23.2.en: Do not be carried along with customs prevailing in society or widespread fears, lest you anger God in ignorance, for these are shadows of pagan worships. Rely on Him, confident of His care and His power, for He protects you so that you may live in peace.

19.24.0.en: He commands them to respect the elderly by standing before them until they allow them to sit down, for respecting the old man (the hoary head) is respect for God and the fear of Him.

19.25.0.en: He commands them to treat the stranger well and to love him like the ordinary citizen, indeed to love him as they love themselves. And to increase their sympathy toward strangers, He reminds them of the suffering of being a stranger that they endured in the land of Egypt, so that they may have compassion on strangers and treat them well.

19.26.1.en: Ephah: a measure for grain equal to about 23 liters.

19.26.2.en: Hin: a measure for liquids equal to about 5 liters.

19.26.3.en: He requires them not to wrong others, not only in the judgments of the courts but in all dealings of buying and selling: they use just balances, and likewise the weights, that is, the metal pieces, are correct, not less when they sell or greater when they buy. Also the use of just measures such as the ephah and the hin, noting that there are correct standards in the sanctuary by which to check them.

19.27.0.en: God commands them to follow all His statutes and not to neglect any commandment, but to take care to apply it and not merely to know it, for the sake of the fear of God, who repeats His name "I am the Lord" sixteen times in this chapter.

19.27.1.en: If you feel God before you at all times, you will treat all people well and keep away from every sin, and if you err, you hasten to repentance and to apologize to others, and so you live in peace, pure and clean.

19.27.2.en: Punishments for those who violate the Law
